Thanks for the draft, Rachel — looks good overall. A few technical clarifications and the canary configuration we will use: 

Technical canary plan (concise):
- Traffic ramp: 1% -> 3% -> 5% over first 6 hours, hold at 5% for at least 72 hours before ramp.
- Autoscaling buffer: we will reserve 20% overhead in Dedicated pool for the duration of the canary to avoid cold-start risk.
- KV cache priming: we will pre-warm common prefixes using your synthetic trace; cache hit target >= 85% as listed.
- Model variants: Primary (quantized-8) + Fallback (float16) — automatic routing if latencies exceed threshold for 10m.
- Observability: we will run sampling of full request/response payloads for 1% of traffic into a redacted bucket for quality analysis. SOC2 redaction rules applied.

Canary gates (operational):
- No active SEV incidents, error budget consumption < 10% for core inference services.
- Latency & error gates must be green for two consecutive 24h windows.

I’m attaching the config doc (Canary_Run_Configuration.pdf) with the exact metrics and Prometheus alerts we will use. I recommend scheduling a dry-run test this week (30–60 minute mini-canary on a low-traffic slice) so we validate observability hooks and rollbacks.

If Veridian agrees, I’ll own the canary execution and run the post-mortem template; Rachel will be the escalation owner for commercial decisions.

—
Neha Kapoor
